standard_prerequisites.name: Recursion principle of the circle
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a type A with a point a : A and a loop p : a = a there is f : S^1 -> A with f(base) := a and ap f (loop) = p; the non-dependent computation rule for loop is what turns the dependent datum into a path.
standard_prerequisites.use: The inverse direction at source line 338 is defined by the circle recursion principle applied to the pair (b, l), and the first round trip at source line 340 is exactly its computation rule.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness principle for maps out of the circle
standard_prerequisites.statement: If f, g : S^1 -> A come with p : f(base) = g(base) and a dependent path over loop between ap f (loop) and ap g (loop), then f(x) = g(x) for all x : S^1.
standard_prerequisites.use: The second round trip at source lines 341-342 is proved by this uniqueness principle, applied with p := refl(base); its hypothesis is discharged by the recursion computation rule.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverses give equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function is an equivalence as soon as it has a two-sided homotopy inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two homotopies f o g ~ id and g o f ~ id at source lines 340-342 are exactly the data that the final sentence at source line 343 feeds into this characterization.

core_obligations: Define the canonical comparison map f : (S^1 -> A) -> (Sigma x:A, x = x) by f(g) := (g(base), ap g (loop)) and note that it is the forward direction of the claimed equivalence (source line 337).
Define the candidate inverse g : (Sigma x:A, x = x) -> (S^1 -> A) by circle recursion, sending a pair (b, l) to the map that takes base to b and whose action on loop is l (source line 338).
Prove the first round trip f o g ~ idfunc: unwind the composite on a pair (b, l) and reduce both coordinates by the computation rule of the recursion principle (source line 340).

Prove the second round trip g o f ~ idfunc, which is not a computation but an appeal to the uniqueness principle: supply p := refl(base) and the dependent path (g o f)(loop) =^{lam x. x = x}_{refl base} loop produced by the recursion computation rule (source lines 341-342).
Conclude that f has a quasi-inverse and is therefore an equivalence, which is the statement (source line 343).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the two directions: the canonical map (g(base), ap g loop) and its candidate inverse built by circle recursion.
First round trip in the sigma type, by the recursion computation rule.
Second round trip as a homotopy of maps out of the circle, by the uniqueness principle with basepoint component refl(base).
Conclude the equivalence from the quasi-inverse.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.2.9 at source lines 330-335: for every type A the canonical map f(g) := (g(base), ap g (loop)) from S^1 -> A to Sigma x:A, x = x is an equivalence. The author's nine-line proof (source lines 336-344) is not a routine unwinding of a definition: the inverse at line 338 goes through the recursion principle of a higher inductive type, the first round trip at line 340 is settled by the recursion computation rule, whereas the second round trip at lines 341-342 cannot be computed at all and needs the uniqueness principle for maps out of S^1 together with its dependent-path hypothesis supplied by the same computation rule. The two round trips therefore live in two different types and are discharged by two different principles, and only the last line records that a quasi-inverse suffices for the equivalence.

compared.difference: That item counts the encode-decode computation of the fundamental group of the circle, pi_1(S^1) = Z, from section 6.2 of the same chapter. The present item is the earlier Lemma 6.2.9, the universal property (S^1 -> A) ~ Sigma x:A, x = x, which the encode-decode section cites as background; it contains no successor covering, no code family and no winding number.

The recursion principle (Lemma 6.2.5) is a different labelled statement from the universal property (Lemma 6.2.9): the recursion principle produces a map S^1 -> A from a point and a loop, while the universal property identifies the whole function type S^1 -> A with the sigma type of based loops. The recursion principle is used as a prerequisite here, not counted again.
